analysis:
Examined the new ServingReadiness.swift (head 1-178), the ProviderLogger.swift enum additions (head 147-149) and the ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift tick hook (head 82).

ServingReadiness is a local diagnostic. It derives a verdict from daemon state (coordinatorConnection, trust, authorization, appAttest and addonHold) and grants no routing or authorization. The coordinator remains authoritative (TB-011, T-052, T-053). The verdict text reflects the coordinator-supplied reason string only in operator-facing status output; it is not written to public logs. The default branch at line 125 echoes the raw reason, but that string is coordinator-trusted. The doc comment at line 9 states the verdict is advisory only.

The new ProviderOperationalMessage cases are fixed strings with only the {cli} substitution. They keep the closed public-log vocabulary and leak no identifiers (T-058).

The capacity tick now calls superviseServingAuthorization() before writeDaemonState (head line 82). Its implementation is not in this batch. The log message at ProviderLogger line 149 implies it may re-register the connection after 15 minutes without authorization.

Questions for integration:
- Verify that re-registration reuses the existing endpoint-resumption and registration path (T-053, A-008). It must not mint new identity or extend proof lifetimes.
- Verify that it is rate-limited, cannot loop or create availability churn, and respects add-on holds (TB-012, T-059).
- Verify that it does not interrupt in-flight inference.
- Verify that its hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization check is not used as local serving admission (T-052).

No regression is identified in the supplied units.
